chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Sama'ah from Abu Basir who said:

I asked: A man performed the obligatory Tawaf, but he did not know whether he had performed six, seven, or eight circuits. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat his Tawaf until he is certain.' I said: But he performed it while offering voluntary (Tawaf al-Nafilah) as well, eight times, and he was forgetful. He said: 'Let him complete it with two additional circuits and pray four Rak'at. As for the obligatory one, let him repeat it until he completes seven Shawat (circuits).'

And joining (performing without break) between the circuits in Tawaf, if it is the obligatory Tawaf, is not permissible. And if it is a voluntary Tawaf, there is no harm in joining between them as much as he wishes. And it is preferable to separate between every two Tawafs with Salat, if the situation is one of choice. He narrated what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one is unsure whether they performed six or seven circuits during Hajj Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of doubt (*shakk*) in Tawaf, distinguishing between obligatory and voluntary circuits to determine whether one must repeat the entire act or simply complete the count. It establishes the principle that while joining circuits is permissible in voluntary Tawaf, it is invalid in obligatory Tawaf unless separated by prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual worship. The ruling underscores the scholarly view that uncertainty in core pillars requires verification to ensure the validity of the act.
